title: Charging Lapse Days on a Late Named Non-Owner Policy Renewal While the Company Stayed Certified
content:
**Principle.** On a Named Non-Owner Policy renewal term accepted after expiration, the share of the term charged follows the company's exposure during the lapse. Exposure is read from the named insured's SR-22 or FR-44 Operator certificate that was on file during the lapse, as the Financial Responsibility Filings (SR-22 / FR-44) records show. The FR-44 form is read before the SR-22 form. For a form, the filings tried are, in this order, its filed filing recorded first, its cancellation-filed filing recorded first and its terminated filing recorded first; the first of these whose filing date is on or before the first lapse day recorded on the term is the one read. Its **certified-through date** is the earlier of its required-through date and its certificate end date; a date not recorded leaves the other, and there is none when neither is recorded.

**Charging rules.**

1. *Certified on every lapse day.* When the certified-through date is on or after the last lapse day recorded on the renewal term, or there is none, the company stayed certified on every lapse day. The charging share is one, a flat full-term charge, and the premium-written entry is booked from the renewal term's effective date with the renewal term's days as its days.
2. *Certified through part of the lapse.* When the certified-through date is on or after the first lapse day but before the last lapse day, the company stayed certified only through that date. The charged days are the renewal term's days less the lapse days after the certified-through date, those days running from the day after the certified-through date, which is included, to the last lapse day, which is included. The charging share is the charged days divided by the renewal term's days, and the entry is booked from the renewal term's effective date with the charged days as its days.
3. *Every other case*, including no such certificate: no lapse day is charged, and the share is the days in force — from the day after the last lapse day, included, to the expiration date, excluded — divided by the renewal term's days.

**Case table (hypothetical; renewal term of 182 days, lapse recorded on its days 1 to 8).**

| Certificate read | Required-through date | Certificate end date | Certified-through date | Charging share | Entry days |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FR-44, filed, filed before day 1 | none recorded | none recorded | none | one | 182 |
| FR-44, cancellation filed, filed before day 1 | years after the term | day 20 | day 20 | one | 182 |
| SR-22, terminated, filed before day 1 (no FR-44 qualifies) | years after the term | day 5 | day 5 | 179 divided by 182 | 179 (lapse days 6 to 8 not charged) |
| SR-22, filed, filed before day 1 | day 8 | none recorded | day 8 | one | 182 |
| FR-44, cancellation filed, filed before day 1 | years after the term | the day before day 1 | before the lapse | days in force divided by 182 | 174 |
| only an FR-44 filed on day 3 | — | — | — (filed after the first lapse day) | days in force divided by 182 | 174 |
